subject: English
title: Class 8 English Olympiad — Paper 1
instructions: The time allowed for this paper is 60 minutes.
This paper contains 50 objective-type (multiple-choice) questions carrying a total of 60 marks.
There is no negative marking for wrong answers.
Each question has four options; choose the one correct answer.
Section 1 and other regular sections carry 1 mark per question; the Achievers Section carries 3 marks per question.
Use of calculators is not permitted unless specified.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'cheerful'.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He is interested ___ music.
Identify the correctly formed question tag: He is smart, ___?
Choose the synonym of 'enormous'.
Fill in the blank with the correct modal: You ___ wear a helmet while riding a bike.
Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to hit the books'.
Choose the correct conjunction: She was hungry, ___ she ate quickly.
Identify the correctly written sentence.
options: Everyone has submitted their assignments only.
Everyone has submitted his or her assignment.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form: This road is ___ than that one.
Choose the word that best completes the sentence: His ___ remarks hurt her feelings.
Identify the error in the sentence: 'He don't know the answer.'
Fill in the blank: The class ___ going on a trip next week.
Fill in the blank: Neither the manager nor the workers ___ satisfied.
Choose the correct word: The news ___ shocking.
Identify the correct reported speech: She said, 'I will help you tomorrow.'
options: She said that she would help me the next day.
She said I will help you tomorrow.
She said that she helps me tomorrow.
She said that she will help me tomorrow.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They are building a bridge.'
options: A bridge has been built by them.
A bridge is being built by them.
A bridge is built by them.
A bridge was built by them.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: By next month, he ___ his project.
Choose the correctly spelled word.
Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to spill the beans'.
Fill in the blank with the correct article: She bought ___ umbrella.
Choose the correct plural form of 'mouse' (the animal).
Choose the word closest in meaning to 'courageous'.
Fill in the blank: If she ___ hard, she would pass the exam.
Choose the correctly spelled word.
Choose the antonym of 'humble'.
Fill in the blank: She is proud ___ her achievements.
Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
Identify the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I need the following items: pen, paper, and glue.
I need the following items, pen paper and glue.
I need the following items; pen, paper, and glue
I need the following items pen; paper, and glue.

questions.question: Choose the correct word: Each of the boys ___ a bicycle.
Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am busy.'
options: He said that I am busy.
He said that he was busy.
He said that he is busy.
He said he will be busy.

questions.question: Read: 'The astronaut described seeing Earth from space as a moment that changed how she viewed her home planet forever.' What effect did this experience have on her?
options: It made her afraid of space travel
It made her indifferent to the environment
It gave her a new perspective and deeper appreciation for Earth

questions.question: Read: 'The librarian created a 'mystery book' display where covers were hidden, encouraging students to choose books without judging them by appearance.' What was the librarian's intention?
options: To reduce the number of visitors
To encourage students to explore books beyond their usual preferences
To make the library more confusing

questions.question: Read: 'The young artist painted the same tree every day for a year, capturing how it changed through the seasons.' What does this show about the artist's approach to art?
options: Patience and attention to gradual change over time

questions.question: Read: 'The teacher used real-life examples like cooking measurements to explain fractions, making the lesson easier to understand.' What teaching strategy is described?
options: Connecting abstract concepts to familiar real-life examples

questions.question: Read: 'The coach reminded the team before every match that losing gracefully mattered as much as winning.' What value is the coach emphasizing?
Read: 'Even after breaking his leg, the young cyclist continued training on a stationary bike, determined to return to racing.' What quality is highlighted here?
options: Resilience and determination to overcome setbacks

questions.question: Read: 'Kabir spent his summer vacation teaching younger children in his neighbourhood to read, refusing any payment for his time.' What quality does Kabir show?
options: Generosity and a willingness to help others

questions.question: Read: 'The old fisherman knew every current and tide of the bay, having sailed it for over fifty years.' What does this passage suggest about the fisherman?
options: He has deep, experience-based knowledge of the bay

questions.question: Read: 'The young chef refused to follow a single recipe twice, believing that creativity came from experimenting with new flavours each time.' What value does the chef prioritize?
Read: 'The scientist's notebook was filled with failed experiments, each one crossed out and followed by a new idea.' What does this reveal about the scientific process?
options: Failed experiments are always wasted effort
Discovery often involves trial, error, and persistence

questions.question: Read: 'Despite the power cut, Sana continued her homework using a small torch, determined not to fall behind in her studies.' What trait does Sana display?
Read: 'As the train pulled into the station, memories of childhood summers spent at grandmother's house flooded back to Aryan.' What is the tone of this passage?
Read: 'The two rival teams, after years of competition, finally joined forces to win the inter-school championship together.' What does this passage suggest about teamwork?
options: Rivalry is always more effective than teamwork
Collaboration can achieve what rivalry alone could not

questions.question: Read: 'The company launched a new policy allowing employees to work from home twice a week, aiming to improve work-life balance.' What is the goal of this policy?
options: To help employees balance their personal and professional lives

questions.question: Read: 'Though the twins looked identical, their personalities couldn't have been more different — one loved adventure, the other preferred quiet reading.' What contrast does this passage highlight?
options: Physical similarity versus difference in interests/personality

questions.question: Which sentence best uses a rhetorical question to persuade readers about the importance of reading?
options: 'Some people read and some do not.'
'Isn't it amazing how a single book can change the way you see the world?'

questions.question: Identify the tone of the sentence: 'Fantastic, my bike has a flat tyre right before the race.'
Read the two statements: (1) 'She seldom complains.' (2) 'She almost never complains.' What is the relationship between them?
options: They convey a similar meaning in different words
Statement 1 is much stronger than statement 2

questions.question: A student must summarize a lengthy article into one clear sentence without losing the main idea. Which skill is being tested?
options: Concise synthesis of the main idea

questions.question: A paragraph repeatedly switches between past and present tense while describing the same event. What editing skill would fix this?
options: Maintaining consistent verb tense throughout the passage
